title: Exact dimer ground states of long-range spin chains and ladders
abstract: Interacting spin chains and ladders are known to support a plethora of quantum phases with complex ground-state phase diagrams. In this work, we study a large family of such models and determine precise, explicit conditions under which an exact dimer state is guaranteed to be the ground state. These general conditions are validated for various generalizations of the Majumdar-Ghosh model using exact diagonalization. Our results provide exact reference points in the phase diagrams of a wide class of spin chains and ladders, including those with anisotropic and arbitrary-range interactions.
summary: This work rigorously determines the conditions under which long-range quantum spin chains and ladders possess an exact dimer ground state. By analyzing Hamiltonian structure using semi-positivity criteria and extending these methods to anisotropic interactions, the authors map out complex phase diagrams. The findings provide both theoretical boundaries and numerical confirmations for understanding highly correlated magnetic phases.
main_problem: The primary goal is determining precise, explicit conditions on coupling constants that guarantee an exact dimer state is the ground state for long-range interacting spin chains and ladders.
main_result: The authors derived sufficient conditions ($\alpha_n \ge 0$, $ eta_{2n} \ge 0$, and $ eta_{2n-1} = 0$) that define regions in the phase diagram where the dimer state is guaranteed, extending these results to anisotropic interactions.
method: The analysis combines theoretical derivation of necessary/sufficient conditions (e.g., semi-positivity arguments) with validation using exact diagonalization on finite systems and geometric interpretations via convex cones.
model_or_system: The study focuses on interacting quantum spin chains and ladders described by long-range Hamiltonians, which are generalized to include anisotropic interactions ($\gamma_\mu$). The system is analyzed in terms of pseudospin operators and related linear exchange models.
key_observables: Ground state energy ($E_{	ext{GS}}$), Dimer entanglement entropy ($\Delta S_{	ext{dimer}}$), and the coefficients $\alpha_n$ and $ eta_n$ derived from the Hamiltonian structure.
important_parameters: Coupling constants $\{J_n\}$ and $\{K_n\}$, anisotropy parameters ($\gamma_x, \gamma_y, \gamma_z$), and system length $L$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an even length $L$ for simplicity; while sufficient conditions are derived, numerical results suggest the actual dimer phase can extend beyond these theoretical boundaries.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing predicted vs. numerically found regions for the dimer state in both isotropic and anisotropic chains/ladders, using energy and entanglement entropy as diagnostics.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing general Hamiltonian forms (chains/ladders) to deriving necessary conditions via semi-positivity arguments ($\alpha_n,  eta_n$). It then extends this analysis to include anisotropy by analyzing the spectrum of an asymmetric quantum top and finally validates results using ED on specific models.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework used—defining physical phases through convex cones and spectral positivity—provides powerful tools applicable to understanding stability in complex, interacting many-body systems beyond simple mean-field treatments.
